mars_sites.name: Amazonis / Arcadia Planitia (AP-8)
mars_sites.why_they_match: Dry permafrost over shallow ice-cemented ground, like AP-8's ice table a few cm down

conditions.label: Terrain
conditions.text: Flat mid-latitude plains on the Arcadia / northern Amazonis boundary; brain-coral and polygonal terrain (~9,000 polygons mapped)
conditions.evidence_quote: We have mapped and measured ∼9,000 thermal contraction polygons.

conditions.label: Elevation
conditions.text: Northern lowlands — low, which helps landing

conditions.label: Thermal
conditions.text: Mid-latitude: cold enough to keep ice near the surface

conditions.label: Solar / power
conditions.text: Mid-latitudes get enough sunlight for solar power

conditions.label: Water / ice
conditions.text: Ice table estimated 8–12 cm deep; ice <1 m below the surface

earth_analogs.label: Amazonis / Arcadia Planitia (AP-8)
earth_analogs.analog: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Beacon, University & Victoria valleys)
earth_analogs.matches: Dry permafrost, buried excess ice and sublimation polygons like AP-8's polygonal, ice-rich ground
earth_analogs.does_not_match: Warmer, wetter and denser air than Mars

workbook_citations: Luzzi et al. 2025, JGR Planets (doi 10.1029/2024JE008724) via USGS & Univ. of Mississippi summaries

mars_sites.name: Mawrth Vallis
mars_sites.why_they_match: Thick, colourful clay-rich layers formed from altered volcanic material

conditions.label: Terrain
conditions.text: Dichotomy boundary: ancient flood channel, 25 km crater, mesas and knobs; drops toward Chryse Planitia
conditions.evidence_quote: It is also older and more weathered, and is dominated by a large 25 km-wide impact crater with a partly collapsed wall and a smaller crater inside at its central point (a central pit).

conditions.label: Mineralogy
conditions.text: Fe/Mg/Al-rich clays up to ~200 m thick (most widespread clays on Mars) under a dark volcanic cap
conditions.evidence_quote: The region is thickly coated in light-toned clays containing silicate minerals; these deposits – some 200 m deep in places – are the most widespread found on Mars, and are obviously visible in these new images (and clearest in the annotated version).

conditions.label: Elevation
conditions.text: ~2 km below datum; hemispheres here differ by up to 3 km

conditions.label: Thermal
conditions.text: Thermal inertia mapped by TES (coarse)

conditions.label: Solar / power
conditions.text: 46 kWh minimum seasonal solar+wind surplus — worst of 24 sites

conditions.label: Water / ice
conditions.text: Water flowed ~3.6 billion years ago; no modern ice noted
conditions.evidence_quote: In fact, we know that liquid water did once run through Mawrth Vallis around 3.6 billion years ago.

earth_analogs.label: Mawrth Vallis

earth_analogs.label: Mawrth Vallis
earth_analogs.matches: Jarosite, gypsum, halite and clays together, like Mawrth's salty layer
